name: CBT-i Coach
summary: Free mobile app from the VA/DoD that supports Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I): sleep diary, education, relaxation tools, and reminders.
description: CBT-i Coach helps users track their sleep, learn CBT-I techniques (sleep hygiene, stimulus control, relaxation), and follow a structured program to improve sleep. Intended as a companion to therapist-delivered CBT-I, but can also be used alone as a self-help tool.
patient_summary: CBT-i Coach provides tools to track sleep and improve habits, such as logging sleep times, relaxation exercises, sleep-friendly routines, and educational materials about sleep behavior. It’s useful for people with insomnia or poor sleep patterns, but not a replacement for therapy if you have complex mental health needs.

linked_conditions.context: CBT-i Coach supports CBT-I protocols — the first-line recommended treatment for chronic insomnia. It can help users track sleep and apply behavioral changes to improve sleep quality. Should be used along with a clinician when possible. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

contraindications: Severe sleep disorders requiring medical intervention (e.g. untreated sleep apnea)
Active suicidality — not a crisis intervention tool

efficacy_data.metric: Improved adherence to CBT-I homework and facilitation of standard CBT-I treatment protocol
efficacy_data.comparison_data: Use of CBT-i Coach vs standard paper-based CBT-I homework (no published RCT specifically measuring superiority)
efficacy_data.patient_text: CBT-i Coach is intended to help you follow standard CBT-I treatment recommendations (sleep diary, stimulus control, sleep hygiene, relaxation) — research supports CBT-I itself as effective for insomnia. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

exclusions: Sleep apnea or untreated medical sleep disorders (should see a sleep specialist)
Active suicidal ideation or psychiatric crisis

sections.heading: What CBT-i Coach Does
sections.text: CBT-i Coach provides tools and education to support Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I). It includes a sleep diary, sleep hygiene tips, relaxation exercises, reminders, and guidance to help reset sleep patterns and build healthy bedtime routines. The app was developed by the VA in collaboration with DoD and academic sleep researchers. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

sections.heading: Effectiveness & Use of CBT-i Coach
sections.text: CBT-i Coach is designed to augment therapist-delivered CBT-I by facilitating homework completion (sleep diary, stimulus control, scheduling). While there is no published RCT showing superior outcome compared to non-app CBT-I, clinician surveys report that many find it helpful and that it improves homework adherence and treatment engagement. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
sections.patient_text: Using CBT-i Coach can help you stay on track with your sleep therapy, keep a precise sleep diary, follow recommended routines, and apply CBT-I tools daily — which are key for improving insomnia.

sections.heading: Who Should Use CBT-i Coach
sections.text: CBT-i Coach is best for adults who:
items: Have chronic insomnia or persistent sleep difficulties
Are undergoing or considering cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I)
Want to track sleep and apply behavior-based tools to improve sleep hygiene
Prefer a free, easy-to-use, evidence-informed tool on their phone
Need support to follow through with homework and self-care between therapy sessions
not_recommended: People with untreated sleep disorders (e.g. sleep apnea, restless legs)
Those in a mental health crisis or with active severe psychiatric symptoms
Users requiring immediate professional sleep medicine interventions
Night-shift workers or individuals with irregular sleep schedules not suited to standard CBT-I recommendations

items.description: Log bedtimes, wake times, sleep quality, awakenings, naps, and sleep-related behaviors daily. Visual sleep charts help identify patterns and measure progress.
Guides on optimizing sleep environment, reducing stimulants, and improving bedtime routines. Helps you understand sleep mechanisms and insomnia maintenance factors.
Includes guided breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, and audio wind-down exercises to help you relax before bed or when you can’t sleep.
Customizable reminders for bedtime, wake time, sleep diary entries, and relaxation practices — supports adherence to consistent sleep schedule and CBT-I homework.

sections.heading: Cost & Access
sections.text: CBT-i Coach is free and publicly available. It was developed by the VA / DoD and is offered at no cost to users. There are no subscription fees or paywalls.
free_features: Full access to sleep diary, education, relaxation tools, reminders
sections.insurance: Not applicable — free publicly available self-help app

sections.heading: Privacy & Data Security
sections.summary: CBT-i Coach stores data locally on your device. The app does not automatically transmit sleep diary or personal data to VA unless you choose to export and share it with a clinician. Use device-level security to protect your data; HIPAA rules don’t apply unless you manually share data with your provider.
items: Sleep data remains on the user’s device unless exported manually
No automatic data sharing or cloud upload by default
Encryption depends on device security settings
Recommended: enable device lock / encryption if available

sections.heading: How to Start Using CBT-i Coach
steps: Download CBT-i Coach from the App Store or Google Play (free)
Open the app and complete the initial sleep questionnaire to assess your sleep patterns
Enter your regular bedtimes and wake times to establish baseline sleep diary
Set up bedtime and wake reminders to encourage consistent schedule
Start tracking your sleep daily and use relaxation exercises if needed
If you plan to start CBT-I with a clinician, bring your sleep diary to sessions to support treatment
tips: Use the sleep diary every morning for best adherence
Stick with the same wake time even on weekends to stabilize circadian rhythm
Avoid alcohol, caffeine, heavy meals, or screens 1–2 hours before bedtime
Use relaxation tools as part of a consistent wind-down routine
If insomnia persists, consult a sleep medicine specialist — insomnia may need professional assessment
common_mistakes: Skipping daily sleep diary entries (makes tracking unreliable)
Trying to ‘fix’ sleep too fast — CBT-I works over weeks with consistency
Mixing frequent naps or irregular schedules — undermines sleep consolidation

items.comparison: Insomnia Coach — a related app by VA for users who are not in formal CBT-I, offering self-guided weekly sleep training and education.
Sleepio — a fully digital CBT-I program with structured weekly modules and automated guidance, though may require subscription or institutional access.

faqs.a: CBT-i Coach is a free mobile app developed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and DoD to help people manage insomnia using evidence-based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) tools like sleep diary, sleep hygiene, relaxation, and routines.
Yes — it is publicly available at no cost, with no subscription fees or paywalls.

faqs.q: Do I need a therapist to use CBT-i Coach?
faqs.a: CBT-i Coach is designed to be used alongside therapist-delivered CBT-I, but it can also be used as a self-help tool. If you have chronic insomnia, use it as part of a structured treatment plan if possible.

faqs.q: Does CBT-i Coach replace therapy or medication?
faqs.a: No. It’s a support tool. For complex or severe insomnia, comorbid disorders, or safety concerns, you should consult a sleep specialist or mental health provider.

faqs.q: Can CBT-i Coach help with chronic insomnia?
faqs.a: Yes. CBT-I (the therapy model behind CBT-i Coach) is considered first-line treatment for chronic insomnia by sleep medicine experts. The app helps you apply CBT-I principles consistently. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
